blocking_defects.criterion: contact_and_consequence (believable agent performing the contact); brief: check physical scale and upper-arm/forearm lengths, reject stretched reach
blocking_defects.defect: New in correction 1. The attendant hands that now perform every gurney, transfer, drape and sheet move are drawn at hs = ks*1.15 with a straight sleeve from local x 58 to len 900, widening to 80 units, and no elbow or upper arm. Against the patient on the same rig: the hand is about 85 table units long, 19 percent of the 440-unit patient (a real hand is about 11 percent of body length). The sleeve is 92 units thick at its far end, thicker than the lying patient's 76-unit silhouette (a forearm is about a third of chest depth). In drape-stamp-medium (medium window, ks .81, hs .93), the right drape hand grips at about (457,924) with dir -28. Its sleeve stays straight for about 650 px to the right frame edge (about 3 m at the patient's scale of roughly 209 px per metre). The left hand at about (391,917), dir -152, runs about 440 px straight to the left edge. The two arms leave opposite frame edges about 1.3 m apart, which no single attendant can do, though the code comment says 'an anonymous attendant'. The same construction drives clock-marker-close (guide), turnover-marker-view split (sheet), table-drape-medium and the s3 vignettes (slide and drape hands). Required result: hands at believable scale for the patient and gurney (about 11 percent of body length), with a forearm that bends at a visible elbow or leaves frame within about one forearm length. If two arms come from opposite sides, show them as two attendants. Check every rig and scale used.

blocking_defects.criterion: contact_and_consequence (continuous identity; the object exists before the agent handles it)
blocking_defects.defect: Residual from review 1. caseGroup draws the drape only when S.drape > 0, while the drape hands are drawn from drapeHands independently. In s2 (drape-stamp-medium), drapeHands has enter 1 from the cut at 10.773 s, but s2-event-3 starts at 10.915 s, so for 0.142 s two pinching hands hold nothing and the folded bundle then pops into their grip. In s3 the hands start descending at b1+0.35 = 14.604 s and only reach the bundle's corners at 15.054 s, but the bundle pops into existence at the s3-event-2 start (14.838 s) while the hands are still about 0.47*520*ks above it (about 200 px in table-drape-medium). The drape therefore appears from nothing and hangs unsupported before its handler arrives. Required result: draw the folded bundle (drapeShape(0)) whenever drapeHands is active, and have it arrive in the hands or rest on the screen bar before the hands take it. It must never appear at event start.

The gurney is first seen emerging from behind the hand on its way to the table. The identical patient shape and gurney re-enter through the same door about 0.14 s after the turnover exit, so viewers may read it as the same patient returning. A visible difference would help. blocking_defects.defect: The attendant's hands and straight, elbowless sleeves are drawn at about 1.7 times hand scale and up to about 3 m of forearm against the patient. That is the agent of every physical step from entry to draping.
The folded drape pops into existence at event start, before or apart from the hands that handle it (s2 at 10.773 to 10.915 s; s3 at 14.838 to 15.054 s).
The result card covers the lit Turnover tag in the closing close shot, and the surgical light head covers the start of the box question in the final wide.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain, from code (not observed): a generic Houston cardiothoracic operating room lights up while its four wall cameras power up and scan, then light in turn and watch a gloved attendant wheel a patient to the doorway. A camera pulse stamps Patient entry as the gurney crosses the threshold, Draped as hands lay the drape, and Turnover as the draped patient leaves and a fresh sheet is laid. The next patient is wheeled in and draped, and a 'Patient draped' text reaches a surgeon's phone. On the suite's records desk the study card shows the suite pulling away from other Houston Methodist sites, with 25 tiles, 7 percent and 8.3 to 41.0. Eleven equal placebo units are stamped short of significance, then 'associated, not caused', bundled reviews, a minority stake and future work tagging turnover. The film closes on a blank turnover box beside the clock and a card of about 25 more a month linked to the rollout, the camera lamps still lit.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on cameras visibly powering up in the room, which serves the question 'add surgeries, or only count them?'. It answers at s7 (about 25 more, associated not caused) and closes on the open turnover box beside the 25-case result card with the cameras still watching. The causal arc now holds. The remaining defects are in execution: the agent's scale, the drape's appearance and closing-label occlusion.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2-shot-2 to s2-shot-3 (10.773 s). The cut jumps from the close threshold crossing to a medium shot of the patient already on the table, where two oversized arms from opposite frame edges pinch empty air for 0.14 s before the drape bundle appears. The transfer is elided by the cut and the new agent's construction breaks the believable handoff.
